name: Tax Identification Number (JTB TIN)
issuer: the State Boards of Internal Revenue (and the FCT Inland Revenue Service)
note: Nigeria's sheet (its government's own sheet on the OECD's automatic-exchange portal ('Information on Tax Identification Numbers'; the OECD's index page sits behind a bot check and wasn't opened, the sheet itself came straight back)), read 2026-10-30: individuals in employment are given their TIN by the State Boards of Internal Revenue or the FCT Inland Revenue Service (the JTB TIN), purely numerical and 10 digits; the FIRS issues it to the armed forces, police, diplomats and companies (8 digits, a hyphen and 0001, not modelled). One TIN serves every tax. Read as given on starting work, to workers. No check rule, age, fee or time is stated.

sources.title: OECD AEOI portal, Nigeria: Information on Tax Identification Numbers (the jurisdiction's own sheet)
sources.said: Individuals in employment are given TIN by the States Board of Internal Revenue/Federal Capital Territory Inland Revenue Service (JTB TIN) ... while that of the JTB is purely numerical and contains 10 digits.
